dominant_themes: Unity and integrity of the nation
scope_boundary: This chapter covers the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, including its text, ingredients, key words, significance, judicial status as part of the Constitution, and amendability. It does not cover other parts of the Constitution in detail except where referenced (e.g., Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles). Foreign constitutions are mentioned only for comparative purposes (e.g., US, Switzerland, Britain). Post-1976 amendments beyond the 42nd are out of scope.

natural_clusters.label: Text of the Preamble
members: Full text of the Preamble as amended in 1976

natural_clusters.label: Ingredients of the Preamble
members: Nature of Indian State (sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, republic)

natural_clusters.label: Significance of the Preamble
members: Views of Pandit Thakur Das Bhargava (soul, key, jewel, yardstick)
Views of M. Hidayatullah (resembles Declaration of Independence)

natural_clusters.label: Preamble as Part of the Constitution
members: Berubari Union case (1960) – Preamble not part of Constitution
Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) – Preamble is part of Constitution
LIC of India case (1995) – reaffirmed as integral part
Not a source of power nor prohibition

natural_clusters.label: Amenability of the Preamble
members: Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) – amendable but basic features cannot be altered
42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) – added Socialist, Secular, Integrity
